summary: sync (internal/cli/sync.go) has a third parent-keyed dependent alongside performance/workout_details: classes_detail, which fetches GET /api/ride/{ride_id}/details and writes the result into the SAME "classes" family record the flat catalog sync already created (via db.UpsertBatchWithFacts, the same write-through path a live `classes show`/`classes structure` call uses, including its nested ride.id id resolution -- see classes-show-nested-ride-id-write-through.json). It differs from the other two dependents in two structural ways a future regen must preserve: (1) its parent ids come from db.ListField("workouts", "ride_id") -- the distinct classes an account holder actually took -- not from the classes resource's own stored ids (tens of thousands in a full catalog sync, which would defeat the point of scoping this fan-out); (2) its "already done" check (planClassDetailSync) is content-based (db.ProviderFactIDsWithField("classes", "segments")), not presence-based, because every taken class already has a "classes" provider_payloads row from the flat catalog sync -- a presence check would see it as permanently done despite never carrying segments/target_metrics_data. "classes" cascades into "classes_detail" the same way "workouts" cascades into performance/workout_details (expandSyncResourcesWithDependents), so a bare `sync` or `workflow archive` picks this up automatically. runDependentFanOut gained an optional `write` parameter (nil defaults to the old db.UpsertWithFacts(resource, id, data) behavior) specifically so classes_detail could report under the "classes_detail" event name while writing into the "classes" family -- any future dependent that needs a different report-name/write-family split should reuse this parameter rather than hardcoding a third resource-name-doubles-as-family-name assumption into the fan-out engine.
reason: A round-11 live verification report (NEW 1, marked highest priority) found that synced classes carry no segments or target_metrics_data for 99.8% of a real account's store (98 of 48,743): the bulk classes catalog endpoint (/api/v2/ride/archived) returns a list shape -- title, duration, instructor_id, ratings, stream URLs, pedaling offsets -- and segments/target_metrics_data only ever come from the per-class detail endpoint, which nothing synced. This made offline_classes_structure/offline_intervals caveat almost every class with "stored class has no comparable segment list", which read as "this class has no segments" when the truth was "this class was synced in list form and its segments were never fetched" -- the report's exact wording. The report offered two options: cascade classes into a bounded/resumable detail fan-out scoped to taken classes (~600 on the reporting account out of 48,743 in the catalog), or at minimum distinguish the two caveat cases. Both were implemented: the dependent sync closes the gap for real, and classSegmentsMissingCaveat (see offline-classes-list-form-caveat.json) still distinguishes list-form-never-fetched from genuinely-empty for classes not yet reached by a bounded backfill.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestPlanClassDetailSync_ScopesToDistinctRideIDsNotFullCatalog asserts the candidate set is exactly the taken classes (workouts.ride_id), never the untaken catalog. TestPlanClassDetailSync_PendingIsContentBasedNotPresenceBased asserts a list-form class (provider_payloads row present, no segments) is pending while a detail-form class (segments present) is not. TestSyncClassDetailDependent_EnrichesExistingClassRecordInPlace drives a fake detail response through the real fan-out and asserts the SAME classes/ride-a provider fact gains a segments field (not a new record under a different key), and that a replan afterward reports it no longer pending. TestProviderFactIDsWithField_DistinguishesPresenceFromFieldPresence (store package) covers the new store method directly, including a segments:null row correctly counting as "missing". TestExpandSyncResourcesWithDependentsCascadesFromWorkouts extended to cover the classes->classes_detail cascade.
